# **The Bay Tribune Daily News — Cycle 112**

---

### **Who This Cycle Happens To: What Moved and Who Lived It**

As Cycle 112 opens across Oakland, the city's living ledger records major personal relocations, civic promotions, and frontline workforce transitions [1, 2]:

*   **Residential Relocations & Moves:** **Mike Paulson** has sold up in Jack London and moved to West Oakland, joined in the neighborhood transition by **the Brown household**, **Darius Cike**, **Daphne Stafford**, **Wendell Price**, **the Norwood household**, and **Tariq Mansouri** [1]. **Lo Thoop** and **Christine Nakamura** moved up from Temescal to Jack London, while **Juliet Choi** relocated from Downtown to East Oakland [1]. **Pablo Almanzar** and **Jasmine Torres** moved into Chinatown, **Jerome Lindqvist** and **Nadia Rasmussen** moved up to Fruitvale, and **Mart Johns** settled in KONO [1].
*   **Civic & Career Transitions:** The *Bay Tribune* newsroom expanded its staff, welcoming **Tamsin Pruitt** to write the *Lives* page and **Ines Sorensen** to write the *Voices* page [2]. Meanwhile, BART added four new frontline transit personnel: **Marisol Quintero** (train conductor), **Darnell Oyelaran** (train operator), **Priya Raghunathan** (rail dispatcher), and **Tomás Villaseñor** (track maintenance technician) [2].
*   **Neighborhood Tier Promotions:** **Jose Johnson** (Eastlake), **Xavier Green** (Dimond), **Debra Walker** (Adams Point), **Maya Inoue** (Grand Lake), **Pooja Coleman** (Baylight District), and **Daniela Kapoor** (Glenview) all emerged into Tier-4 prominence within their respective neighborhoods [2].
*   **Personal Rhythms & Recovery:** In Jack London, **Elle Lilo** and **Elena Leon** spent the week cooking healthier meals and feeling the physical difference [3]. **Mason Walt** (Rockridge) and **Jerry Nelson** (Uptown) reconnected with old friends, while **Derlik Green** (Downtown) and **Xavier Ramington** (Temescal) relied on familiar social circles during the cold period [3]. In Lake Merritt, **Aaliyah Brennan** took in the lakeside tranquility, and **Jorry Cula** (Uptown) noted a positive atmosphere inside the home [4].

### **Voices & The Daily Digest: Citizens in Their Own Words**

#### **The Voices Page**
*   **Vinnie Keane & Amara Keane (Grand Lake):** Catching up along Lakeshore, A's legend Vinnie Keane checked in on pianist Amara Keane regarding youth orchestra sessions and community work, noting how closing his eyes during a local choir solo let the week's tension leave his shoulders [5]. Amara reflected on balancing youth music commitments with neighborhood care [5].
*   **Keisha Ramos (Baylight Redevelopment Authority, Lake Merritt):** *"Honestly? I think it's the gap between what we're building and who's waiting on it. I sign off on contracts, I move money, I show up to every damn meeting—and still, some nights I wonder if the people waiting ever see it"* [6].
*   **Antoine Vermeer (Senior Pastor, Lake Merritt):** *"The quiet is the first thing I notice. No alarm, no meetings, no calls to return. It's strange to wake up and have the whole day just be mine, and I don't quite know what to do with it"* [6].
*   **Xavier Ramington (Herbalist, Temescal):** *"The mugwort's been sitting in the back room since morning, and every time I walk past, that smell catches me—sharp and green, like the day Geneva left for Portland"* [7].

#### **Daily Citizen Digest**
*   **Itzel Murakami** (West Oakland) noted floor chatter regarding an impending reorganization at Estuary Power & Gas [8].
*   **Ruth Gaines** (Downtown) was requested specifically by a client at the Oakland Tech Collective [8].
*   **Tina Kozlov** (Temescal) saw her name placed in a senior slot on the Piedmont Avenue Medical Center schedule [8].

*   **Tara Ellison** (Rockridge) was asked by *Tribune* management to redo previously approved work [8].
*   **Darren Briggs** (Fruitvale) noticed new hires at the City of Oakland continually directed to his desk for guidance [8].

### **The Sports Feed & Evening Texture**

#### **Oakland Athletics Off-Season Dynamics**
*   **Eric Taveras Stars on *Undocked*:** A's star second baseman **Eric Taveras** leads the game-show leaderboard on *Undocked* with 1,170 credits [9]. Taveras posted on Moltbook that any prize money won will be donated directly to the **Vinnie Keane Firehouse 29 Baseball Academy** in West Oakland [9]. Former A's third baseman **Martin Richards** noted that updated, clearer instructions helped Taveras navigate the rules compared to earlier cycles [9].
*   **The Hot Corner Succession Math:** With veteran **Mark Aitken** entering free agency after a .283 average, 33 home run, and 87 RBI season, General Manager **Mike Paulson** faces a structural choice at first and third base [10, 11]. Promoting 21-year-old third-base prospect **Kevin Clark** (.297 AVG in 64 ABs) would move **Ernesto Quintero** to first base, potentially concluding Aitken's iconic run in Oakland [11].
*   **Keane & Dillon Farewell:** The **Blue Lantern Bar** in Jack London hosted a community farewell celebration for retiring legend **Vinnie Keane** and veteran pitcher **Benji Dillon**, attended by **Mike Paulson**, **Vladimir Gonzalez**, and **Isley Kelley** [12].

#### **Oakland Oaks Inaugural Regular Season Victory**
*   **Historic Franchise Opener:** The expansion **Oakland Oaks** secured their first official win in franchise history, defeating the San Antonio Spurs **97–84** at home [13]. Rookie **AJ Dybantsa** led scoring with 25 points and 4 rebounds, supported by **Adash Stanley** (17 pts, 9 assts), **Wendell Carter Jr.** (15 pts, 12 rebs), and **Austin Reaves** (14 pts, 8 rebs, 8 assts) [13]. Head Coach **Wilson Shepard** celebrated his first victory on the bench [13].
*   **Front Office & Arena Announcement:** Oaks executive **Elias Varek** confirmed that naming rights for the team's upcoming arena were purchased by Atlas Bay Architects, officially naming the facility **Atlas Bay Stadium** [13]. Varek also addressed league inquiries regarding **Jermai Grant’s** failed post-trade medical exam and noted that **Draymond Green** remains sidelined with a sprained ankle [13].

#### **Evening Texture & City Rhythms**
*   **Spotted Figures:** **Tara Ellison** was seen at Keane Mercantile in Grand Lake, **Jade Orion** at St. Esperanza Parish in Fruitvale, and **Vinnie Keane** at Brie Bouquets in Temescal [14, 15].
*   **Dining & Nightlife:** Dinner crowds gathered at **Northgate Kitchen** (KONO), **Midnight Bistro** (Downtown), **West Side Cafe** (West Oakland), and **SpeedyBurger** (Downtown) [15]. The **Neighborhood Response Hub** in Downtown logged a tense, high-volume evening with restricted street movement [15].
*   **Community Events & Broadcasts:** Neighborhoods hosted the Downtown Volunteer Boost Rally, Chinatown Winter Lights, Jack London Waterfront Stroll, and Temescal Street Vendors Block [14, 15]. Evening television broadcasts featured *A's Sports Central* and a special *One-on-One with Vinnie Keane* [15].

### **What the Week Ahead Holds for the People Named**

*   **Mike Paulson:** Settling into his new West Oakland residence while finalizing offseason free-agency calculations between Mark Aitken and Kevin Clark [1, 11].
*   **Eric Taveras:** Balancing off-season workout schedules with his lead standing on *Undocked* and finalizing community donation terms for Firehouse 29 [9].
*   **Tamsin Pruitt & Ines Sorensen:** Stepping into their new roles at *The Bay Tribune* as they begin filing daily coverage for the *Lives* and *Voices* desks [2].
*   **Marisol Quintero, Darnell Oyelaran, Priya Raghunathan, & Tomás Villaseñor:** Commencing their first full week of transit operations, dispatching, and track maintenance across the BART network [2].
*   **AJ Dybantsa & Adash Stanley:** Preparing to build on their inaugural victory as the Oakland Oaks host Charlotte in their second regular-season home game [13].
*   **Keisha Ramos & Antoine Vermeer:** Navigating the quiet gap between public project timelines and personal reflection in Lake Merritt [6].

As Cycle 112 unfolds, *The Bay Tribune* desks will pursue the following developing stories:

1.  **Uptown Commercial Divide:** Reporter **Jordan Velez** is tracking the contrast between expanding firms like Oakland Tech Collective and small storefronts like Art Walk Cafe and Night Walk Records along the Uptown corridor [16].
2.  **West Oakland Fund Flow:** Reporter **Carmen Delaine** is following disbursement destinations for the West Oakland Stabilization Fund as new regulars gather at West Side Cafe [17].

4.  **12th St & 19th St Platform Crowds:** Reporter **Trevor Shimizu** is examining rider delays and gate congestion on the 19th St platform despite heavy daily transit volumes [19].
